answers.reason: Statement carries the obligation with its exceptions, retail-sale scope and public-accessibility condition; mandatory.

The package referred to is the one required only when the product is accessible to the public while held for sale; the statement restates the scope with exceptions but drops that condition (it appears nowhere, not even in the condition label).
Statement adds a verification duty ('and confirm it does') not in the paragraph, and drops the public-accessibility condition of the package requirement.
Requires sealing of two-piece hard gelatin capsules covered by the section with acceptable tamper-evident technology in addition to the package; mandatory, OSD only.
Statement reproduces the lead-in obligation with its purpose and exceptions; the sub-paragraph attributes are separate items.
Sub-paragraph (i) with its lead-in: the statement must identify all tamper-evident features and capsule sealing technologies; mandatory.
Sub-paragraph (ii) with its lead-in: statement prominently placed; mandatory.
Sub-paragraph (iii) with its lead-in: statement placed so it is unaffected if the feature is breached or missing; mandatory.
Conditional requirement to refer to the identifying characteristic in the labeling statement is stated fully; mandatory.
Permissive 'may request an exemption' stated as optional, matching the text.
Exemption requests must be submitted as a citizen petition; mandatory, nothing added or omitted of substance.
'Should be clearly identified on the envelope' rendered as recommended envelope marking.
Petition content (1) with mandatory lead-in, product name or class name plus product list.
Petition content (2): reasons compliance is unnecessary or cannot be achieved; mandatory.
Petition content (3): alternative steps available or taken to reduce malicious adulteration; mandatory.
Petition content (4): other justifying information; mandatory.
NDA holders must notify FDA of packaging and labeling changes made to comply; the change-reporting reference paraphrases the cited rule.
'May be made before FDA approval' stated as optional, matching the text.
Capsule-sealing manufacturing changes require prior FDA approval; mandatory, OSD scope appropriate.
Examination during finishing operations for correct labels stated fully; mandatory, applies to all plant types.
Representative sample at completion of finishing operations, visually examined for correct labeling; mandatory.
Results of the (a) and (b) examinations recorded in batch production or control records; mandatory.
Expiration date determined by appropriate stability testing to assure standards at time of use; mandatory.
Expiration dates related to labeled storage conditions as determined by stability studies; mandatory.
Reconstituted products: expiration information for both reconstituted and unreconstituted forms; mandatory.
Expiration dates on labeling per FDA expiration-date labeling requirements; mandatory.
The text grants the exemption outright ('are exempt ... provided that'), not a permissive 'may'; labeling it optional and phrasing it as 'may be exempt' misstates its force.
Investigational products reconstituted at dispensing must bear expiration information for the reconstituted product; mandatory.

Statement summarises the sub-paragraphs but omits their qualifiers (release by the quality control unit; temperature, humidity and light so identity, strength, quality and purity are not affected), so it is incomplete.
Procedures must include quarantine until quality control unit release; mandatory via lead-in.
Procedures must include storage under appropriate temperature, humidity and light so product attributes are not affected; mandatory.
Statement summarises the sub-paragraphs but omits the permitted temporary and appropriate deviation from oldest-stock-first and the 'readily determined' qualifier, so it is incomplete.
Oldest approved stock distributed first, with the temporary and appropriate deviation allowance; mandatory via lead-in.
System so distribution of each lot can be readily determined to facilitate recall; mandatory via lead-in.
